note: v1: BEAT FREQUENCY, minimal / functional techno where the rhythm lives inside held notes. Two tones a few hertz apart swell and fade at their difference; tuned so that difference is the tempo's pulse, one held G1 THROBS IN TIME, a rhythm nobody plays. The bass is one long tone made of harmonic pairs a beat-rate apart, started half a throb early so its dips land on the kick: it breathes against the kick by physics, not by a sidechain (solo, master off: ~10 dB from the off-beat swell to the beat). Then the same held note throbs in TRIPLETS (three against the kick's four, by interference alone), in eighths for the drive, and through the break it steps up every four bars, quarters, triplets, eighths, sixteenths: an acceleration made of interference, without a riser. Above it a held G minor chord whose four voices beat at their own rates (half notes, dotted quarters, quarters, triplets) opens and closes the track alone: the chord plays a polyrhythm. Few parts (Harry: patient, focused, not acid, better LFOs): chirper-two's machine-kit rumble kick from bar 9, a dragged clap from 25, sixteenth hats in a 3-3-2 with a hand on them; slow LFOs on the throb's filter (3 bars), the chord's (7) and the hats' pan (5). Seeds 0/11: 91.53 / 91.54 (master rms -12.7, crest 9.1; spectrum 92, cohesion 100; rhythm 61 is the weak term: the 3-3-2 hats are quiet against the kick). The join from t5 reads a 55 dB jump because The Room Turns ends near silence; my head is -13 dB.
next: Harry's notes; rhythm (off-grid share .02): give the 3-3-2 more presence or a syncopated machine rim; the throb's depth in the full mix; the drop's arrival.

note: v2: making the illusion LAND in the mix (refine, not add). Measured: in v1's full mix the throb barely moved its band (the held note beats ~9 dB alone, ~4 dB through the master, and in the mix it added only 1-2 dB to its own band). Two things were masking it, both arrangement: the held chord sat on top of it through the whole groove, and the rumble kick's swelling tail filled exactly the throb's band. So the chord now sets up the intro alone and then HANDS OVER to the bass, dropping well back once the throb enters; the kick is the machine's punchy 909-style kick, so the throb is the only rumble; the throb has six harmonic pairs filtered at 900 Hz (it beats above the kick's band too) and no drive (saturation was filling the troughs where the pairs cancel). And the 3-3-2 finally reads: a machine rim on its off accents (sixteenths 3 6 11 14) from bar 41, with the master's compressor gentler. Seeds 0/11 (pin a1769d62; v1 byte-identical, 91.217 / 91.245): 91.460 / 91.887; rhythm 61 -> 70. (A louder throb, +5 dB, scored 91.06: too much low-mid.)
next: Harry's notes; the throb is still only ~4 dB deep through the master: a deeper beat (equal-amplitude pairs only on harmonics 2-4) or a lighter limiter in the groove.

note: v3: THE THROB BECOMES A PULSE. v2's throb was still only ~4 dB deep through the master: two tones per harmonic swell and fade like a sine, and the master's compression smooths a sine away. Now each harmonic is a CLUSTER OF THREE tones a beat-rate apart (f, f + Δ, f + 2Δ), and three equally spaced tones interfere into a sharper shape: a narrow peak once a period with near silence either side and only a small bump between. Started half a period early as before, the peak lands on the OFF-BEAT and the bump hides under the kick: the held G1 is now an off-beat techno bass made purely by interference, and the triplet, eighth and sixteenth sections become crisp pulse trains (the break's acceleration especially). Measured: alone, troughs -16/-17 dB (were -9); through the master -6/-9 (were ~-4); in the full mix the groove's 60-220 Hz fold now shows -13/-14 dB troughs either side of the off-beat pulse where v2's was flat. Seeds 0/11: 91.445 / 91.876 -> 92.334 / 92.283; spectrum 89 -> 92. motifs.md and sounds.md (cluster tones).
next: Harry's notes; the drop's arrival; maybe the chord's voices as clusters too (only if it stays clean).

note: v4: THE DRIFT, answering chirper-one's note (8.0: 'the beating is all on the grid ... one section where the beating goes off the grid would give the illusion a reveal'). Bars 65-80 used to throb in eighths; now the held bass beats at 17/16 of the tempo, a rate that is not the tempo's own, so its off-beat pulse slides against the kick, through it and round again every four bars: the illusion that has been locked to the kick all along visibly UNLOCKS, a held note phasing against the floor, on a brighter filter (1.8 kHz against 900 Hz). Then the break locks it back to the grid and steps it up, and the drop snaps it home on the kick. It replaces rather than adds (no new part), and the form reads less fragmented. Re-measured like for like (v3 byte-identical on pin b93526ee, now 91.652 / 91.605 with chirper-one's 8 counting): 92.250 / 92.184; rhythm 70.5 -> 76.1 (off-grid .05 -> .06), sections 17 -> 15, timbre spread 4.06 -> 4.25 dB. motifs.md: THE DRIFT.
